blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A partner wants your messages in jPOS's <isomsg> XML form, each preceded by a four-digit ASCII length. Your link today runs ASCIIChannel with the 1987 ASCII packager. What has to change?

options.text: Only the packager, to XMLPackager, since ASCIIChannel writes its four-digit length in front of the XML form
options.says: 16.1: the packager produces the bytes and ASCIIChannel only puts four digits of length in front of them; the run shows 0197 followed by the XML.

options.text: Only the channel, to XMLChannel, since XMLChannel writes the XML form and a four-digit length in front of it
options.says: 16.1: XMLChannel has no length header; it frames by reading up to the closing </isomsg>, and the XML itself comes from the packager.

options.text: A new channel subclass whose send method writes the XML, since framing and encoding belong in one class
options.says: 16.1: the packager encodes and the channel frames, so a different pair in the configuration is enough; no new code.

options.text: A new channel subclass whose header methods write the length, since ASCIIChannel's length counts ISO fields only
options.says: 16.1: ASCIIChannel counts whatever the packager produced, XML included (0197 in the run).

origin.section: 16.1. Another Syntax Changes the Packager, Not the Messages

questions.stem: Your switch sends purchases to a partner as JSON over HTTPS, and the partner's API answers each one in the same HTTP exchange; it takes no idempotency key. A purchase of 40.00 gets no answer within your timeout. What should the switch do?

options.text: Send the purchase again, since an API that answers in the same exchange has applied only what it answered
options.says: 16.1: a JSON 0200 means what it meant in unit 4: with no answer its outcome is unknown, and a resend can make the cardholder pay twice.

options.text: Send the purchase again, since a JSON request carries no STAN the partner could take for a duplicate
options.says: 16.1: the fields and their meaning don't change with the syntax, and resending an unanswered purchase can make the cardholder pay twice.

options.text: Reverse the purchase, since the partner could have approved it before the answer was lost
options.says: 16.1: the outcome is unknown exactly as in unit 4, and reversals come with the messages whatever the syntax.

options.text: Decline it locally and send nothing, since the partner could have declined it before the answer was lost
options.says: 16.1: with no answer the outcome is unknown, so the partner could equally have approved it; forgetting the purchase leaves the cardholder paying for a sale the merchant reported as failed.

origin.section: 16.1. Another Syntax Changes the Packager, Not the Messages

questions.stem: Your server unpacks a partner's XML messages with XML2003Packager and answers each 0800 by cloning it. One 0800 starts with a DOCTYPE that declares an entity naming a file on your server, and field 48 refers to that entity. What happens?

options.text: The message is refused, since jPOS packagers parse a partner's XML with DOCTYPE declarations turned off
options.says: 16.3: only XMLPackager refuses a DOCTYPE; XML2003Packager turns that check off in its constructor.

options.text: The message is refused, since an authenticated link only delivers XML that the partner's own parser has checked
options.says: 16.3: message text is input from another system even on an authenticated link; the receiving parser has to refuse DOCTYPE declarations.

options.text: The file's content goes back in field 48, since this packager lets the parser resolve the entity before the clone
options.says: 16.3: XML2003Packager reads the file into field 48, and a server that answers echoes by cloning the request sends it back.

options.text: The file's name goes back in field 48, since this packager keeps entity references as text without reading them
options.says: 16.3: the run shows field 48 holding the file's content, not the reference.

origin.section: 16.3. An XML Parser That Accepts a DOCTYPE Reads Files for the Sender

questions.stem: A bank that has moved its instant and high-value payments to ISO 20022 asks a card processor when its own link to the card network will move as well. Which answer matches where the standards stand?

options.text: Soon, since the card networks follow the plan that moved banks off the SWIFT MT messages
options.says: 16.4: the move off SWIFT MT concerns cross-border payments between banks; card authorization is still overwhelmingly ISO 8583.

options.text: Soon, since ISO 20022 already defines card messages from acquirers to issuers
options.says: 16.4: ISO 20022 defines card messages, but authorization between acquirers, networks and issuers still runs on ISO 8583.

options.text: Not for now, since card authorization between acquirers and networks still runs on ISO 8583
options.says: 16.4: card authorization between acquirers, networks and issuers is still overwhelmingly ISO 8583; the bank's payments and the card link run on different standards.

options.text: Not for now, since ISO 20022 defines no card messages that acquirers and networks could use yet
options.says: 16.4: ISO 20022 does define card messages, from acceptor to acquirer and from acquirer to issuer.

origin.section: 16.4. ISO 20022 Models the Business First, and It Carries Account-to-Account Payments

questions.stem: A gateway receives ISO 20022 card payments and forwards them on a 1987 link with jPOS's ASCII packager. One merchant's structured name and town together take 47 characters. What should happen to field 43?

options.text: Let the packager cut it to 40, since a fixed-length field keeps the first 40 characters
options.says: 16.5: the packager refuses the 51-character value with 'error packing field 43'; it cuts nothing.

options.text: Let the packager pad or cut it, since it fits every value to the field's defined length
options.says: 16.5: the packager refuses a value that is too long, at run time, so the message isn't sent.

options.text: Shorten it in the mapping as the network specifies, since the packager refuses longer values
options.says: 16.5: someone has to decide what to cut and how the network wants name, town and country laid out in 40 characters; the mapping is agreed field by field.

options.text: Move it to a private field in the mapping, since field 43 can't hold a name and a town
options.says: 16.5: field 43 holds the name and location in 40 characters; the mapping decides how they fit, with the network.

origin.section: 16.5. A Bridge Between the Standards Decides, Field by Field, What the Other Side Lacks

concepts: A translation between the standards is a field-by-field mapping agreed with the other party, because the packager refuses what doesn't fit and one side lacks data the other expects.
ISO 20022 defines messages from a business model and carries account-to-account payments, while card authorization between acquirers, networks and issuers stays on ISO 8583.
A new syntax is a packager paired with a channel that frames it, and the messages keep their flows: an unanswered request is still reversed, whatever the syntax.
XML from a peer is parsed with DOCTYPE declarations and external entities refused; XML2003Packager in 2.1.7 resolves them and can read a local file into a field.
